newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan punishes officials entertained by oil trader.
newsitem.headline: Japan punishes officials entertained by oil trader.

text.p: Six senior officials of the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) have been reprimanded for accepting excessive favours from an oil broker arrested on suspicion of tax evasion and for failing to supervise staff properly, Japan's Trade Minister Shinji Sato told a news conference on Thursday.

Millionaire oil wholesaler Junichi Izui, owner and sole employee of oil wholesaler Izui Oil Co., has boasted of his close ties with powerful figures, and domestic media have reported that he wined and dined politicians and bureaucrats.
The Trade Ministry, which is in charge of overseeing the oil industry, has come under fire over the allegations of close ties between the oil dealer and senior officials.
"I strongly regret that this case has dampened public trust," Sato said. "But I was relieved that none of the officials questioned did favours for Izui."
Sato announced that Vice MITI Minister Tsutomu Makino would his salary cut for two months.
Sato said he has instructed an internal committee to come up with new disciplinary guidelines regarding contacts with people in the industries the ministry oversees.
"Until then, the ministry has banned all staff from dining with industry people they are concerned with," Sato said.
Other MITI officials who were reprimanded include the secretary to the trade minister and the head of the Agency of Natural Resources and Energy, an arm of MITI.
Some 100 high-ranking officials and department heads of the Trade Ministry were questioned in the investigation.
Izui was arrested last month on suspicion of evading 310 million yen in taxes.
